land.text: the part of Lan Na's 1362 shape inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape ('some of its territory', the Chiang Saen and Mekong lands)

predecessors.note: Chiang Saen and the Mekong lands ceded after Phayu's defeat (Lan Xang page, no year; 1353 is the Lan Na dossier's date).

land.text: the northern Khmer lands (Isan north of the Mun and the Mekong valley), as Cliopatria draws their passage to Lan Xang

predecessors.note: Isan north of the Mun and the Mekong valley, from the Khmer Empire in Cliopatria's 1363 row; the Lan Xang page has Fa Ngum cross the Khorat Plateau to Roi Et after 1357 and does not say the Khmer ceded it.

land.text: the western uplands of the 1362 Đại Việt shape that lie inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape ('Xam Neua and several smaller Đại Việt towns')

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's 'Ngô Dynasty' row also holds the Trần-era Đại Việt; the Lan Xang page says Fa Ngum 'took Xam Neua and several smaller Đại Việt towns' (no year).

land.text: Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) and Vieng Chan (Vientiane), tributaries of Sukhothai in Cliopatria's 1294-1362 shapes

predecessors.note: The Sukhothai dossier has the Lao kingdoms of Muang Sua and Vieng Chan break free c.1298-1299; Fa Ngum then took Muang Sua, its king his uncle.

land.text: Luang Prabang, where Kitsarat's coronation in 1707 created the Kingdom of Luang Prabang

successors.note: The Kingdom of Vientiane page does not say how the provinces were shared; the north is my reading.

land.text: Vientiane and the centre, 'converting Lan Xang into the Kingdom of Vientiane'
the southern part of Lan Xang, which seceded

successors.note: Champasak page: 'founded in 1713 when the southern part of the Lan Xang seceded' under Nokasad; 1707-1713 it is Vientiane's south.

capitals.name: Xieng Dong Xieng Thong (Luang Prabang)
capitals.note: Infobox: Luang Prabang 1353-1560; Muang Sua is 'alternately' Xieng Dong Xieng Thong. The page also says the court moved to Vientiane in 1533 under Photisarath, but the formal move was 1560.

capitals.name: Viangchan (Vientiane)
capitals.note: 'In 1560, King Setthathirath formally moved the capital of Lan Xang from Luang Prabang to Viangchan.' Burmese-held Jan-Aug 1565 and Feb-Apr 1570, and occupied by the Burmese from 6 December 1574 to April 1575; from 1575 to 1591 the city lies inside Lan Xang's outline under Burmese suzerainty (a vassal king, Chao Tha Heua, then Sen Soulintha).

rulers.name: Fa Ngum
rulers.note: 5 January 1353 to 1372 on the list; the Fa Ngum page has the infobox reign 1353-1372 and the text 'In 1373 ... exiled him'.

rulers.name: Samsenethai (Oun Huan)
rulers.note: The list gives 1372; the first pass of this dossier met 1368 and 1372 for his accession on different pages. The Fa Ngum page has his birth in 1357.

rulers.name: Phommathat
rulers.note: Reigned 10 months [citation needed on the list].

rulers.name: Yukhon (Meunsai)
rulers.note: Reigned 8 months.

rulers.name: Khon Kham
rulers.note: Reigned 18 months.

rulers.name: Kham Tam Sa (Kham Teun, Khamtum)
rulers.note: The list gives 1429(?) and 1432 and leaves the end blank: 'Reigned 5 months'.

rulers.name: Lusai
rulers.note: Reigned 6 months.

rulers.name: Kham Keut (Kham-Kert, Kham Keul)
rulers.note: Illegitimate son of Samsenethai [citation needed].

rulers.name: Nang Keo Phimpha
rulers.note: The list leaves the end blank; an interregnum 1438-1441 (rule by Sena and members of the Sangha) follows.

rulers.name: Chakkaphat Phaen Phaeo
rulers.note: Killed when Luang Phabang fell in fall 1479 (Le Thanh Tong page).

rulers.name: Souvanna Banlang
rulers.note: [citation needed on the list]; the Lan Xang page has him crowned in 1479.

rulers.name: Somphou
rulers.note: 1495-1497 under regency by his uncle.

rulers.name: Photisarath I
rulers.note: To 8 August 1548.

rulers.name: Setthathirath
rulers.note: From 8 August 1548; also king of Lan Na 1546-1551. The Bayinnaung page has him killed 'sometime before mid-1572'.

rulers.name: Nokeo Koumane
rulers.note: First reign, as a baby under regency.

rulers.name: Sen Soulintha
rulers.note: First reign; the Bayinnaung page has him withdraw from Vientiane before 6 December 1574 and be handed to Bayinnaung later.

rulers.name: Voravongsa I (Maha Oupahat, Chao Tha Heua)
rulers.note: Burmese vassal. The Bayinnaung page (Laotian history) has Maha Ouparat die in 1580; the Lan Xang page: 'he would rule only four years'.

rulers.name: Sen Soulintha
rulers.note: Second reign, as a Burmese vassal (Lan Xang page: 'In 1580 Sen Soulintha returned as a Burmese vassal').

rulers.name: Nakhon Noi
rulers.note: Not of royal descent. An interregnum 1583-1591 [citation needed on the list] follows, the years of the civil war.

rulers.name: Nokeo Koumane
rulers.note: Second reign; crowned in Vientiane in 1591 and cast off allegiance to the Toungoo Empire.

rulers.name: Voravongsa II (Thammikarath)
rulers.note: Nephew of Setthathirath.

rulers.name: Oupagnouvarath
rulers.note: Son of Voravongsa.

rulers.name: Photisarath II
rulers.note: Son or grandson of Sen Soulintha; not of royal descent.

rulers.name: Mon Keo (Mongkeo)
rulers.note: Son of Voravongsa.

rulers.name: Tone Kham
rulers.note: Son of Mon Keo.

rulers.name: Vichai
rulers.note: Son of Mon Keo.

rulers.name: Souligna Vongsa (Sourinyavongsa)
rulers.note: The list: 1638-1694, '2nd Golden Age of Lan Xang'; the Sourigna Vongsa page has 1637-1694.

rulers.name: Tian Thala
rulers.note: Not of royal descent; the senior minister who usurped the throne, six months.

rulers.name: Nan Tharat
rulers.note: Grandson of Vichai.

rulers.name: Setthathirath II
rulers.note: Nephew of Souligna Vongsa. The list's partition table has Kingkitsarat at Luang Prabang from 1706 (to 1713; backed by Sipsong Panna) and Setthathirath II (Sai Ong Hue) at Vientiane 1707-1730 (backed by Hue); the state ends in 1707.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1363 but the infobox gives 'Founded by Fa Ngum: 1353' and the lead says Lan Xang 'held the area of present-day Laos from 1353'. The core is Cliopatria's 1363 outline without the 731 northern Khmer cells and the 76 Đại Việt border cells (503 cells: the Lao kingdoms of Muang Sua and Vieng Chan plus the Lan Na cession); the ledger adds those two at 1363. [fix se-01-f] The Lan Xang page's summary sentence 'By 1357 Fa Ngum had established the mandala for the Kingdom of Lan Xang' (from the Sipsong Panna border south to Sambor, and from the Vietnamese border west to the Khorat Plateau escarpment) is the page's latest date for these lands, but it dates no conquest of its own; Cliopatria enters the Khmer and Dai Viet cells only in 1363 and the khmer-empire and ngo-dynasty dossiers carry 1363, so the ledger keeps 1363 at confidence 1.

union.text: the northern Khmer lands (Isan north of the Mun and the Mekong valley), as Cliopatria draws their passage to Lan Xang

correction.text: Lan Xang at its founding: the Lao core, Muang Sua (Luang Prabang), Vientiane and Xiang Khouang with the lands ceded by Lan Na; 'In 1353 Fa Ngum was crowned' and named the kingdom Lan Xang Hom Khao

keyframe_review.note: 375,643 km2. The page gives no area (its infobox has populations only: 400,000 in 1500, 319,000 in 1600, 371,000 in 1700, all 'citation needed'), so no ratio. The outline is Laos plus the Khorat Plateau and the Đại Việt border towns that the page says Fa Ngum took (the plateau 'to Roi Et', 'Xam Neua and several smaller Đại Việt towns'); both are undated on the page and enter at Cliopatria's 1363 in the ledger. Soft edge.

377,339 km2: the 1363 outline within 8 cells added and 4 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin. No dated frontier change on the page for 1375-1384; Samsenthai received Ming recognition in 1402 (page), not a territorial event.

375,702 km2: the same outline (1 cells added and 6 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). The page dates nothing between Samsenthai's accession and 1402; the 1390s fighting with Lan Na at Chiang Saen is undated in extent.
375,921 km2: the same outline (1 cells added and 2 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). Nothing on the page for these years.

375,696 km2: the same outline (3 cells added and 1 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). The page is silent on any 1429-1449 border change; Lê territory beyond the Annamite range is the Lê dossier's. Muang Phuan (Xiang Khouang), inside the outline, entered 'a tributary relationship with the Dai Viet' in 1434 (Muang Phuan page) and was 'annexed' in 1448 (Le Thanh Tong page): the pages disagree and neither says the Lao outline shrank, so it is kept; the Dai Viet claim is drawn as a contest from 1471 (ledger).

375,471 km2: the same outline (1 cells added and 1 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin), kept through the 1479 Đại Việt invasion. 'Luang Phabang was captured' in fall 1479 (Lê Thánh Tông page) but Suvanna Balang was crowned in 1479 and the outline does not change: the invasion is a contest, not a loss (ledger 1479-1484). Muang Phuan (Xiang Khouang) lies inside this outline: Le Thanh Tong 'made that territory a prefecture of Dai Viet in 1471' (Le Thanh Tong page), the Muang Phuan page has Dai Viet 'attempted to annex Muang Phuan as a prefecture' by 1478 and Muang Phuan 'returned as a tributary to Lan Xang' once the Dai Viet army withdrew (undated); the outline is kept and the claim is a contest 1471-1484 in the ledger.
375,507 km2: the same outline (1 cells added and 2 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). Visoun reigned 1500-1520 per the page; no territorial event is dated.
375,477 km2: the same outline (1 cells added and 1 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). Nothing dated on the page for 1512-1528.
375,367 km2: identical cells to 1512-1528. Photisarath reigned 1520-1550; the page says the court moved to Vientiane in 1533 (capital_move noted in the capitals, formal move 1560).
375,339 km2: the same outline (1 cells added and 3 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). The page has Lan Xang defeat an Ayutthaya invasion at Sala Kham in 1540, so no land is lost.

375,313 km2: the same outline (4 cells added and 2 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). Includes the Burmese occupations of Vientiane (2 Jan-1 Aug 1565; Feb-Apr 1570), which are ledger events, not a change of owner; Setthathirath retook Vientiane in 1568 (Bayinnaung page).

356,925 km2 in Cliopatria: 63 cells (Vientiane and the middle Mekong, lon 100.2-103.1, lat 17.3-20.8) pass to the Toungoo shape from 1572, and the shape runs to 1578. The Bayinnaung page has Setthathirath killed 'sometime before mid-1572' (Lao history: 1571), Sen Soulintha refuse Bayinnaung's ultimatum to submit and the Burmese retreat in early 1573, and the Burmese king and his armies enter Vientiane 'on 6 December 1574' without opposition. No page has Vientiane or the Mekong pass to Burma in 1572, and from December 1574 the pages have a vassal king, not an annexation (rule 4: a vassal is a lighter tint, not a change of owner). The whole 1571 outline therefore stands for 1572-1574; 1575-1578 follow in the next keyframe. [fix se-01-f: the 1574 'loss' of the earlier version is withdrawn]

correction.text: Lan Xang unreduced under Sen Soulintha, the 1571 outline, for 1572-1574 (the Burmese entered Vientiane only on 6 December 1574)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1575-1578: the whole 1571 outline (1,310-odd cells, about 375,300 km2), now a Burmese vassal. The Bayinnaung page: the Burmese king 'appointed a younger brother of Setthathirath, Maha Oupahat (Chao Tha Heua), king of Lan Xang with the regnal name Voravongsa I, and returned to Pegu on 16 April 1575'; the Lan Xang page: 'A Burmese vassal, Chao Tha Heua, was left to administer Vientiane, but he would rule only four years' and lists a 'Burmese Colonial Period (1574-1597)'. Cliopatria's 1572 shape (356,925 km2) is the wrong reading of this: it takes 63 cells as Burmese land; the vassal tint (vassal_start counterpart lan-xang 1574-12, vassal_end 1591) belongs in first-toungoo-empire's ledger. [fix se-01-f: correction was the reduced 1572 shape]

correction.text: Lan Xang as a Burmese vassal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1579-1587: Cliopatria has no Lan Xang shape for these nine years because its Toungoo shape of 1579-1587 contains all 1,249 remaining Lan Xang cells, i.e. it annexes a vassal. The Bayinnaung page: 'On 17 October 1579, he sent a sizable army (22,000 men, 1200 horses, 120 elephants), which faced no opposition' because 'instabilities arose in Lan Xang'; according to Laotian history Maha Ouparat died in 1580 and Bayinnaung 'installed Sen Soulintha ... as the successor' (Burmese chronicles 'make no mention of any change'); the Lan Xang page: 'In 1580 Sen Soulintha returned as a Burmese vassal' and 'From 1583 to 1591 a civil war took place in Lan Xang'. The Lao state keeps its whole 1571 outline as a Burmese vassal; first-toungoo-empire should draw it as a tributary tint (vassal_start 1574-12 / vassal_end 1591), and its own 1579-1587 shape should not hold these cells.

correction.text: Lan Xang as a Burmese vassal (the 1571 outline), under Sen Soulintha from 1580 and in civil war from 1583

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria restores the 1,310-cell outline (375,070 km2) in 1588 after nine years inside the Toungoo shape (1579-1587). The land was Lan Xang's throughout: the Lan Xang page has a civil war 1583-1591, and Nokeo Koumane, 'crowned in Vientiane' in 1591, 'cast off any allegiance to the Toungoo Empire' (the independence date; the Bayinnaung page only has every vassal independent by 1599). The outline therefore holds for the whole of 1588-1594, as a Burmese vassal to 1590 and independent from 1591. [fix se-01-f: the earlier version restricted it to 1591-1594]

correction.text: the 1588 outline for 1588-1594: a Burmese vassal in the civil war to 1590; 'In 1591 he was crowned in Vientiane' and cast off allegiance to the Toungoo Empire

keyframe_review.note: 375,288 km2: the same outline (1 cells added and 1 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). Nokeo Koumane 'attacked Lanna in 1593' (Lan Na was a Burmese tributary 1558-1596 per the Lan Na page) and died suddenly in 1596; no land change is dated.

375,426 km2: the same outline (2 cells added and 2 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). The Sourigna Vongsa page (reigned 1637-1694, 'The Golden Age') dates no frontier change; it has Sourigna Vongsa and Narai build Phra That Si Song Rak 'to mark their friendship and set the boundary' (undated) and is silent on any treaty with Đại Việt in 1651.
375,454 km2: the same outline (+1 cell). Nothing dated on the Sourigna Vongsa page for 1648-1652.

375,559 km2: the same outline (2 cells added and 3 removed against the previous shape, all at the margin). Nothing dated on the page; the 1652 marriage to a princess of Xieng Xouang (Muang Phuan) is not a territorial event.
375,316 km2: the same outline (+1 cell). The page gives no frontier change in the long peace to 1694.

The outline is unchanged but the state ends in 1707, not 1708: 'In 1707 Lan Xang was divided' (Lan Xang page), 'The Kingdom of Vientiane was formed in 1707 as a result of the split of the Kingdom of Lan Xang' (Vientiane page); the shape belongs to 1706-1707 only, after which the land passes to Luang Prabang and Vientiane (Champasak from 1713).

ledger.note: 1353: Fa Ngum is crowned and founds Lan Xang Hom Khao at Luang Prabang. 'In 1353 Fa Ngum was crowned' (Lan Xang page); 'In 1353, he conquered Vientiane, Xiang Khouang and then Luang Phrabang' (Fa Ngum page). The Lan Xang page dates the fall of Vientiane to 1357 ('marched on Vientiane in 1356 and took it in 1357'); the two pages disagree and the core keeps all three.

region.text: Muang Sua (Luang Prabang), Vientiane and Xiang Khouang: 'In 1353, he conquered Vientiane, Xiang Khouang and then Luang Phrabang' (Fa Ngum page); the Lao kingdoms that Cliopatria's Sukhothai shape held to 1362

ledger.note: 1353: Fa Ngum defeats Lan Na at Chiang Saen. 'defeated King Phayu of Lanna at Chiang Saen' (Lan Xang page, no year); the Fa Ngum page puts his northern conquests (Muang Sing, Muang Houm, Chiang Hung) in 1352-1354, and the Lan Na dossier carries the matching loss at 1353.

region.text: the part of Lan Na's 1362 shape inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape ('some of its territory', the Chiang Saen and Mekong lands)

ledger.note: 1363: the Khorat Plateau comes into the Lan Xang outline. 'then advanced across the Khorat Plateau to Roi Et' after the fall of Vientiane in 1357 (Lan Xang page, no year); 'By 1357, Lan Xang's mandala reached south to Sambor'. The year is Cliopatria's (its row begins 1363 and the Khmer shape loses these 731 cells that year); the page does not say the Khmer ceded the land. [fix se-01-f] Checked the Fa Ngum page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fa_Ngum): it says only that he conquered 'modern day Isan', undated, and does not mention the plateau. The Lan Xang page dates only the Vientiane campaign (1356-1357) and the summary 'By 1357 Fa Ngum had established the mandala' reaching the Khorat Plateau escarpment, so 1357 is the page's latest date; the ledger keeps Cliopatria's 1363 so that it matches khmer-empire's loss.

region.text: the northern Khmer lands (Isan north of the Mun and the Mekong valley), as Cliopatria draws their passage to Lan Xang

ledger.note: 1363: Xam Neua and the Đại Việt border towns join the outline. 'He took Muang Phuan and then Xam Neua and several smaller Đại Việt towns' (Lan Xang page, no year); the year and the 76 cells are Cliopatria's (the Ngô dossier carries the matching loss at 1363). [fix se-01-f] The Fa Ngum page: he 'conquered western Nghe An as well as the valleys between Red River and Black River in Vietnam (Tonkin)', undated; the Lan Xang page's 'By 1357' mandala sentence also reaches 'the Vietnamese border along the Annamite Range'. The year stays Cliopatria's 1363, matching ngo-dynasty.

region.text: the western uplands of the 1362 Đại Việt shape that lie inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape ('Xam Neua and several smaller Đại Việt towns')

ledger.note: 1471: Dai Viet claims Muang Phuan (Xiang Khouang) inside Lan Xang. The Le Thanh Tong page: 'Back in 1448, the Vietnamese had annexed the land of Muang Phuan' and 'Thanh Tong made that territory a prefecture of Dai Viet in 1471'. The Muang Phuan page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muang_Phuan) disagrees on the years: 'In 1434, Muang Phuan entered into a tributary relationship with the Dai Viet', 'by 1478 the Dai Viet attempted to annex Muang Phuan as a prefecture', and it 'remained part of Lan Xang' in the 16th and 17th centuries. 1471 is the formal act; the region is my reading of the pages' 'Muang Phuan' as the Xiangkhoang province. No Lao land is lost in the outline. le-dynasty has no mirror of this event.

region.text: Muang Phuan (Xiang Khouang), the principality incorporated into Lan Xang under Fa Ngum in the mid-14th century

ledger.note: 1479: Lê Thánh Tông takes Luang Prabang. 'In fall 1479, Thánh Tông led an army of 180,000 men' and 'Luang Phabang was captured and the Laotian ruler Chakkaphat was killed'; the Lan Xang page: Vietnamese forces 'took the capital of Luang Prabang' and the successor was 'crowned as Suvanna Balang (The Golden Chair) in 1479'.

region.text: Luang Phabang, the capital, and its province

ledger.note: November 1484: the Vietnamese war ends. 'By November 1484, Thanh Tong and his forces had withdrawn back to Dai Viet' (Lê Thánh Tông page) after defeats by a combined Lan Xang-Lan Na force; the Lan Xang infobox lists the war as 1479-1484 and no land changed hands. [reviewer se-01-f]

November 1484: the Dai Viet forces are gone and Muang Phuan is Lan Xang's again. 'By November 1484, Thanh Tong and his forces had withdrawn back to Dai Viet' (Le Thanh Tong page); the Muang Phuan page: 'The Dai Viet army ultimately withdrew during that conflict, and Muang Phuan returned as a tributary to Lan Xang' (undated, so the date is the withdrawal's).

1546: Prince Xaysettha of Lan Xang is crowned King of Lan Na. 'The text says he was crowned in 1546' and the Lan Na page has Queen Chiraprapha abdicate in 1546, giving the throne to her grandson; the Lan Xang page dates the coronation in Chiang Mai to 1547. A personal union, drawn as a tint over Lan Na; the Lan Na dossier records the accession as a rename of the dynasty.

region.text: Lan Na under King Setthathirath, 'ruled by a Laotian king'

ledger.note: 1551: the Lan Na nobles choose Mekuti. 'The Nobles of Lanna felt that Setthathirath had stayed away too long, and sought another descendant' in 1551; Setthathirath failed to retake Lan Na in 1553 and took Chiang Saen in 1555 (same page), but the page does not say how long he held it.

region.text: Lan Na after the Lao king's departure

ledger.note: 1560: Setthathirath formally moves the capital of Lan Xang from Luang Prabang to Vientiane. 'In 1560, King Setthathirath formally moved the capital of Lan Xang from Luang Prabang to Viangchan'; the Lan Xang page says the court had moved to Vientiane in 1533 under Photisarath.
2 January 1565: Burmese armies take Vientiane. Three armies led by the crown prince 'easily captured Vientiane on 2 January 1565'; Setthathirath escaped and was chased for months.

1 August 1565: the Burmese leave Vientiane. They left on 1 August 1565, installed a son-in-law of Setthathirath as vassal king and took Maha Ouparat to Pegu; Setthathirath's forces retook Vientiane in 1568 (same page).

February 1570: Bayinnaung's second army drives Setthathirath from Vientiane. 'Bayinnaung personally led a two-pronged invasion in October 1569' and Setthathirath 'held Vientiane for a few months, then retreated into the jungle in February 1570'. That the Burmese held the city is my reading; the Setthathirath page has 'In 1570 Bayinnaung retreated'.
April 1570: the Burmese give up. 'The search for Setthathirath was called off in April 1570' after many Burmese troops 'died of starvation and disease'.

6 December 1574: the Burmese king and his armies enter Vientiane. 'On 6 December 1574, the king and his massive armies faced no opposition entering Vientiane' because Sen Soulintha had withdrawn to the countryside (he was later arrested and handed to Bayinnaung); the king appointed Setthathirath's younger brother Maha Oupahat (Chao Tha Heua) king of Lan Xang as the vassal Voravongsa I. [fix se-01-f] Lan Xang keeps its whole outline: the pages have a vassal king, not an annexation (the earlier 'loss' of Vientiane and the Mekong is withdrawn). The Burmese suzerainty, 1574-12 to 1591, is a tint in first-toungoo-empire's ledger (vassal_start counterpart lan-xang).

16 April 1575: the Burmese king returns to Pegu. The king 'appointed ... Maha Oupahat (Chao Tha Heua), king of Lan Xang with the regnal name Voravongsa I, and returned to Pegu on 16 April 1575'; the page dates the return to Pegu, not the departure from Vientiane, and does not say how long he stayed (about four months by its dates). The vassal king stays; Lan Xang remains whole under Burmese suzerainty until Nokeo Koumane casts off allegiance in 1591 (Lan Xang page). Other dates of the suzerainty: the army of 17 October 1579 met no opposition; Sen Soulintha returned as a vassal in 1580; civil war 1583-1591.

1707: Kitsarat's coronation at Luang Prabang splits the kingdom. 'In 1707 Lan Xang was divided' (Lan Xang page); 'The Kingdom of Vientiane was formed in 1707 as a result of the split of the Kingdom of Lan Xang', Kitsarat's coronation creating the Kingdom of Luang Prabang. The page does not say how the provinces were shared; the north is my reading of 'Luang Prabang'.

1707: Lan Xang ends, divided between Luang Prabang and Vientiane. 'Kingdom partitioned: 1707' (infobox); 'In 1713 the Kingdom of Champasak emerged' after a rebellion against Vientiane, and Muang Phuan 'also seceded during the following years' (undated).

region.text: the whole kingdom: the north to Luang Prabang, the centre to Vientiane, the south to Champasak from 1713

wars.name: Fa Ngum's conquests

zones.text: the part of Lan Na's 1362 shape inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape ('some of its territory', the Chiang Saen and Mekong lands)

wars.outcome: Fa Ngum took Muang Phuan, Xiang Khouang, Muang Sua and Vientiane, crossed the Khorat Plateau to Roi Et and defeated King Phayu of Lan Na at Chiang Saen, which 'forced Lanna to cede some its territory'.
wars.note: The Fa Ngum page: 'In 1352-1354, he conquered Muang Sing, Muang Houm, Chiang Hung' and 'In 1353, he conquered Vientiane, Xiang Khouang and then Luang Phrabang'; the Lan Xang page dates the fall of Vientiane to 1357. Sipsong Panna (Chiang Hung, Yunnan) is outside Cliopatria's shape and no page dates its loss.

wars.name: Đại Việt invasion of Lan Xang
wars.outcome: Lê Thánh Tông's army of 180,000 captured Luang Phabang and killed the ruler Chakkaphat; Suvanna Balang was crowned in 1479 and Lan Xang kept its territory.
wars.note: The Lan Xang infobox lists the war as 1479-1484; the body does not mention 1484. Muang Phuan (Xiang Khouang), attacked in 1479 and claimed by Dai Viet since 1471, is a second zone; see ledger 1471.

wars.name: Lan Xang-Ayutthaya war of 1540
wars.outcome: Lan Xang 'defeated an Ayutthaya invasion at Sala Kham in 1540'; a treaty of 1563 sealed by a betrothal followed, and no border moved.

wars.name: Lan Xang-Lan Na campaigns of 1553-1555
wars.outcome: 'In 1553 King Setthathirath sent an army to retake Lanna from Mekuti but was defeated'; in 1555 he 'managed to take Chiang Saen'. Lan Na was not retaken.
wars.note: No contest event: the page does not say how long Chiang Saen was held. Bayinnaung invaded Lan Na in 1556 and Mekuti surrendered on 2 April 1558.

wars.name: Burmese invasions of Lan Xang
wars.outcome: Vientiane taken 2 January 1565 and left 1 August 1565; retaken by Setthathirath in 1568; second invasion October 1569-April 1570; after Setthathirath's death Sen Soulintha resisted until the Burmese entered Vientiane on 6 December 1574; Bayinnaung left on 16 April 1575 with Voravongsa I as vassal king. The Burmese then kept Lan Xang as a vassal: the army of 17 October 1579 met no opposition, Sen Soulintha returned as a vassal in 1580, and Nokeo Koumane cast off allegiance in 1591 (Lan Xang page). No Lao land changed hands.
wars.note: The Setthathirath page dates the Burmese arrival at Vientiane only 'after Ayutthaya fell' and speaks of retreats in 1565 and 1570. [fix se-01-f] The 16 April 1575 date is the king's return to Pegu, not his departure from Vientiane.

wars.name: Lao invasions of Cambodia
wars.outcome: 'The Khmer Chronicles record that armies from Lan Xang invaded in 1571 and 1572'; the Khmer king was slain in the second invasion and Lan Xang retreated. No border moved.

wars.name: Lan Xang civil war and end of Burmese suzerainty
wars.outcome: 'From 1583 to 1591 a civil war took place in Lan Xang'; Nokeo Koumane 'was crowned in Vientiane' in 1591, marched to Luang Prabang and 'cast off any allegiance to the Toungoo Empire'.
wars.note: Not a contest over ground: Toungoo is listed as the suzerain whose allegiance was cast off. The Burmese army of 17 October 1579 had met no opposition and Sen Soulintha ruled as a vassal 1580-1582 (Lan Xang and Bayinnaung pages). The vassal tint 1574-12 to 1591 is first-toungoo-empire's.

certainty.note: No page gives a surveyed or treaty frontier. The Sourigna Vongsa page has a boundary with Ayutthaya marked at Phra That Si Song Rak (undated) and 'a series of treaties' on trade and boundaries (undated); the frontier stays soft.

Does not contain 1448 or 1471.

notes: Cliopatria's Lan Xang row is one outline (about 375,000 km2, 1,307-1,314 cells) repeated for 345 years; the 15 shapes that differ from it by 1 to 8 border cells are reported 'ok' and are rounding, not events. The only apparent changes in the row are the 63 cells moved to the Toungoo shape in 1572 and the 1579-1587 gap (the Toungoo shape of 1579-1587 contains all 1,249 remaining Lan Xang cells), restored in 1588. Both are the Burmese suzerainty of 1574-1591, which the pages describe as vassalage, not annexation: the Burmese entered Vientiane on 6 December 1574 and installed a vassal king (Maha Oupahat, Chao Tha Heua), the army of 17 October 1579 met no opposition and Sen Soulintha ruled as a vassal from 1580, and Nokeo Koumane cast off allegiance in 1591 after the civil war of 1583-1591. Lan Xang therefore keeps its whole outline 1572-1590 (keyframes 1572, 1575, 1579, 1588) and the ledger has no loss; first-toungoo-empire must carry vassal_start counterpart lan-xang 1574-12 and vassal_end 1591, and its own 1572-1587 shapes should not hold the cells. Disagreements and silences: the fall of Vientiane is 1353 on the Fa Ngum page and 1357 on the Lan Xang page; the Khorat Plateau and Xam Neua conquests are undated (entered at Cliopatria's 1363 at confidence 1); Fa Ngum's Sipsong Panna (Chiang Hung) conquest is outside Cliopatria's outline and undated; the Lan Xang page lists a 'Burmese Colonial Period (1574-1597)' although it also has independence in 1591; the Setthathirath page and the Bayinnaung page order the Burmese captures of Vientiane differently (the Bayinnaung page was used); Lao and Burmese sources differ on Setthathirath's death (1571 vs 'sometime before mid-1572'). Not settled: the 1471 'prefecture of Muang Phuan' (Lê Thánh Tông page) and the later secession of Muang Phuan (undated on the Vientiane page) need a Muang Phuan dossier; the pages disagree on Muang Phuan (Le Thanh Tong page: annexed 1448, a prefecture of Dai Viet in 1471; Muang Phuan page: tributary to Dai Viet 1434, attempted annexation by 1478, back as a Lao tributary after the Dai Viet withdrawal, still part of Lan Xang in the 16th-17th centuries), so the outline is kept and the claim is a contest 1471-1484 (le-dynasty has no mirror yet; a muang-phuan dossier is needed); the 1707 division of provinces between Luang Prabang and Vientiane is not given by the pages (the north is a reading); the ruler list is the List of monarchs of Laos (identity.rulers), whose dates differ from other pages' in places (Fa Ngum's exile 1372 or 1373, his son's accession 1368 or 1372, Maha Ouparat's death 1579 or 1580). The Sourigna Vongsa page is silent on a 1651 Đại Việt treaty. The Kingdom of Luang Phrabang page was not opened (budget). Slugs used as counterparts that need dossiers from other groups: vientiane, kingdom-of-luang-phrabang, kingdom-of-champasak (se-01 list), post-angkor-cambodia (exists), first-toungoo-empire (se-01, not yet written when this was done), plus Muang Phuan and Muang Sua (named, no slug).
